idea: Simple ways to protect plumbing during renovation
title: Smart Ways to Protect Your Plumbing During a Renovation
description: During a remodel, dust and debris like drywall powder, tile grout, and wood shavings can easily drop into open drain pipes, causing severe blockages deep in your plumbing line long before the project is finished. Protecting your system is straightforward: ensure all open drain lines and water rough-ins are tightly sealed with test caps or expansion plugs until fixtures are ready for installation. Always shut off and tag main water supply valves before demolition starts to avoid accidental pipe punctures from tools. Taking these basic precautions during construction prevents costly line clearing and keeps your plumbing system safe.
image_prompt: A crisp, photorealistic vertical photograph shot on an 85mm lens showing a bathroom undergoing active renovation. In the central foreground, a standard 2-inch white PVC drain pipe extends vertically from a clean subfloor. The top of the PVC pipe is securely sealed with a bright orange plastic rough-in test cap to prevent construction debris from falling inside. Nearby, red and blue PEX water supply lines extend cleanly from an exposed wood stud wall, capped with brass crimp caps. The background features unfinished drywall and structural wood framing in soft, natural lighting with a shallow depth of field. Photorealistic textures of real plastic pipes, concrete subfloor, and timber. No text, no logos, no people, no impossible pipe joints.
